title: A puzzle about communicating vessels: every lever works once, so you have to read the whole order before you touch anything
author: office-canard
selftext:
REBEL LEVEL is a puzzle about communicating vessels. Tanks are joined by pipes. Open a valve and the liquid flows until the levels even out, or until it drops below the pipe. Your goal is to bring the marked tanks to the red line.



The catch is that every lever works exactly once. Open the wrong one first and the liquid goes somewhere you can't get it back from. So the real puzzle happens before you touch anything: reading the order.



A few decisions that shaped it:



\- No hints. You can always reason it out from what's on screen, so a hint would only take that away.

\- No warning when you're stuck. The game doesn't tell you it's over until you've used up every lever. One button, AGAIN, restarts any time, and it only turns into NEXT when you clear.

\- Stacking the tanks in two tiers is what made it a real puzzle. Liquid falling from an upper tank into a lower one changes everything.

\- I wanted it to feel industrial and heavy. The liquid moves like thick oil, the valves are levers, and there's a diamond wire mesh behind the tanks.



256 basins, one screen each, no timer.



How AI fit in:

I made this with Claude (Anthropic's AI), and it wrote all of the code.



\- The basins were generated, not hand-placed. A solver tries every order of levers, and only layouts with exactly one shortest solution survive, ranked by how many first moves are traps. Every build replays all 256 solutions through the real game code to prove each basin can be cleared.

\- All sound, including five music tracks, is synthesized in code. Claude can't hear, so I judged every sound by ear and cut what sounded wrong.

\- The look, the weight of the liquid, no hints, no stuck warning, 256 basins: those were my calls.

\- Some things only showed up on a real phone. A glow on the moving liquid stuttered on Android, so it's gone.
